short: Formant target and hybrid front end (M06) are standard; evaluation (M12) is behind: clip-level formant R2 of one speaker, no measure of the synthesized speech that earlier ultrasound work reported.
position: Ultra2Speech [@saha2020ultra2speech] changes the processing stage (M06) twice: a factorized spatial, temporal and joint 3D-convolution front end with channel shuffling, and the first two formants as the acoustic target where 35 of 50 ultrasound-to-speech studies name spectral vocoder parameters (pattern match, Appendix). The front end is standard: spatiotemporal convolution is the most frequent ultrasound front end. The formant target is a real departure, since no ledger ultrasound-to-speech study first public before it predicts formants (Appendix), but it stays standard: no spectral-target system is trained on its data (Table 1), and the data are vowel sequences only (Sec. 4.1). Evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work: earlier ultrasound-to-speech studies scored synthesized speech on held-out sentences [@hueber2011statistical; @csapo2017dnn; @gosztolya2019autoencoder], while this paper scores only formant regression on randomly shuffled one-second clips of one speaker.
